end.summary:
- Discussed Bishnoi, sacred groves and Chipko as traditional nature-protection practices.
- Explained that roots hold soil and reduce soil washing into rivers.
- Identified sacred groves as places where trees and animals are protected.
- Connected neem leaves with keeping insects away; the science connection needed further clarification.
- Teach-back was not completed successfully.
end.parentNote: Asha practised examples of traditional communities and ways their practices protect trees, animals, water and soil. Dev used the idea that roots hold soil and identified how sacred groves protect living things. There was a mix-up that science means only chemicals, and it was not corrected by the end. At home, ask Dev to explain how one traditional practice can also be explained using science.
